bottom_line: In adults with unstable angina or non–Q-wave acute myocardial infarction, atorvastatin 80 mg/d vs placebo reduced the primary end point (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.00).
implications: Over 16 weeks after an acute coronary syndrome, this trial’s reported numbers support that atorvastatin 80 mg/d (vs placebo) reduced the composite primary end point (14.8% vs 17.4%; RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.00; P=.048), with the document reporting no significant differences in death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or cardiac arrest, and reporting higher abnormal liver transaminases with atorvastatin (2.5% vs 0.6%).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial with 16-week follow-up across 122 centers.
major_points.quote:
Design and Setting A randomized, double-blind trial conducted from May 1997
to September 1999, with follow-up through 16 weeks at 122 clinical centers in Eu-
rope, North America, South Africa, and Australasia.

major_points.text: Patients were adults with unstable angina or non–Q-wave acute MI, randomized 24 to 96 hours after admission to atorvastatin 80 mg/d vs placebo.
major_points.quote:
Between
24 and 96 hours after hospital admis-
sion, eligible patients were randomly
assigned with stratification by center
to double-blind treatment with ator-
vastatin (80 mg/d) or matching pla-
cebo for 16 weeks.

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite including death, nonfatal MI, cardiac arrest with resuscitation, or recurrent symptomatic ischemia with objective evidence requiring emergency rehospitalization.
major_points.quote:
The
primary combined end point was death,
nonfatal acute MI, cardiac arrest with re-
suscitation, or recurrent symptomatic
myocardial ischemia with objective evi-
dence requiring emergency rehospital-
ization.

major_points.text: Primary end point occurred in 14.8% vs 17.4% (atorvastatin vs placebo), with RR 0.84 (95% CI, 0.70-1.00; P=.048).
major_points.quote:
a pri-
mary end point event occurred in 228
patients (14.8%) in the atorvas-
tatin group and 269 patients (17.4%) in
the placebo group (relative risk [RR], 0.84; 95%
confidence interval [CI], 0.70-1.00; P=.048).

major_points.text: No significant differences in death, nonfatal MI, or cardiac arrest; symptomatic ischemia requiring emergency rehospitalization was lower with atorvastatin (6.2% vs 8.4%; RR 0.74).
major_points.quote:
There were no significant differences in risk
of death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or cardiac arrest between the atorvastatin group
and the placebo group, although the atorvastatin group had a lower risk of symptomatic
ischemia withobjectiveevidenceandrequiringemergencyrehospitalization(6.2%vs8.4%;
RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.57-0.95; P=.02).

inclusion_criteria.text: Adults aged 18 years or older with chest pain/discomfort at least 15 minutes at rest or minimal exertion within 24 hours preceding hospitalization, representing a change from usual anginal pattern.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Eligiblepatients were adults
aged 18 years or older with chest pain
or discomfort of at least 15 minutes’ du-
ration that occurred at rest or with mini-
mal exertion within the 24-hour pe-
riod preceding hospitalization and
represented a change from their usual
anginal pattern.

inclusion_criteria.text: Unstable angina required evidence of myocardial ischemia by at least 1 listed criterion (ECG changes, new wall motion abnormality, reversible perfusion defect, or troponin elevation not exceeding 2 times ULN).
inclusion_criteria.quote:
diagnosis
of unstable angina required evidence of

or T-wave changes in at least 2 con-
tiguous standard electrocardiographic
leads, a new wall motion abnormality

inclusion_criteria.text: Non–Q-wave acute MI required elevation of serum creatine kinase (or MB fraction) or troponin exceeding 2 times the ULN.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Diagnosis of non–Q-
wave acute MI required elevation of se-
rum creatine kinase or its MB fraction,
or troponin to a level exceeding 2 times
the ULN.

analysis_methods.text: After blinded pooled data showed lower-than-predicted primary end point occurrence, sample size was increased to 3000 to maintain power for relative treatment effects.
analysis_methods.quote:
Conse-
quently, the steering committee rec-
ommended an increase in sample size
to 3000 patients to maintain 95% power
to detect a 30% relative treatment ef-
fect and 80% power to detect a 25%
relative treatment effect.

analysis_methods.text: Primary combined end point analyzed by time to first event using a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by country and inclusion event.
analysis_methods.quote:
The primary combined end point
was analyzed by time of first event,
using a Cox proportional hazards
model16 stratified by country and
inclusion event (unstable angina or
non–Q-wave acute MI).

analysis_methods.text: All end point analyses were intention-to-treat with all randomized patients included.
analysis_methods.quote:
All end point analyses
were performed on an intention-to-
treat basis, with all randomized
patients included in the analyses.

analysis_methods.text: Protocol specified 3 interim analyses; P=.001 for each interim and final analysis adjusted to P=.049.
analysis_methods.quote:
The study protocol specified 3 in-
terim analyses of safety and efficacy by
the data safety and monitoring board.
A significance level of P=.001 was used
for each interim analysis, with a sig-
nificance level for the final analysis ad-
justed to P=.049
